title: Graph AI raises $13.3 Mn in Series A round led by Insight Partners
summary:
AI powered patient safety startup Graph AI has raised $13.3 million in its Series A funding round led by Insight Partners, with participation from existing investor Bessemer Venture Partners.
The latest round comes nearly a year after the startup raised its seed round in October 2025.
Graph AI will use the fresh capital to expand its presence across the US and Europe and accelerate product development.
Founded in 2024, Graph AI develops Graph Safety, an AI powered platform that automates workflows for pharmacovigilance and patient safety teams in the pharmaceutical and biotechnology sectors.
The platform combines AI with deterministic controls, validation layers, and end to end audit trails to help pharma companies manage safety operations while maintaining traceability and human oversight.
Graph Safety automates processes involved in handling adverse event reports and safety cases. According to the company, its live deployments have reduced case processing turnaround times from more than three hours to under 10 minutes, a reduction of over 90%. The platform has also helped lower operating costs by up to 66%, it claimed.
The startup currently offers two modules, Intake, which captures and triages adverse event reports, and Nucleus, an intelligent safety database that automates case processing. Its third module, Report, focused on automated aggregate reporting, is scheduled to launch this month.
Graph AI said it has onboarded pharmaceutical and biotech customers across North America and other markets. The startup is also working with customers on upcoming products, including Signal, which is designed to identify emerging safety signals and patterns across cases.

title: AI contact centre startup Dialflo raises Rs 1.7 Cr led by AJVC
summary:
AI-powered contact centre startup Dialflo has raised Rs 1.7 crore in its first funding round led by early-stage venture capital firm AJVC. The round also saw participation from angel investors Afsar Ahmad, Jani, and Arpit Dave.
Founded in 2024, Dialflo is building an AI-first contact centre platform for enterprises. The startup combines human agents with AI agents and uses an attribution engine to track actions across both and link them to customer experience and return on investment (ROI).
The company initially started with the ONEST project, where it built voice AI agents to help ITI students prepare resumes. It later expanded to projects involving Smartstaff, Lokal, and other companies.
Dialflo currently serves more than 10 enterprises, including Tata Digital, Intugine, and Careernet.
The startup will use the fresh capital to expand its engineering and AI teams, strengthen its attribution engine, and onboard more enterprise customers.
Dialflo is targeting 20 enterprise customers over the next six months. It plans to focus on India and the Middle East over the next two to three quarters.
The startup competes with Crescendo and Firstsource in the enterprise contact centre space. Unlike pure-play AI or BPO providers, Dialflo is focusing on a hybrid model combining human and AI agents.
The company has not disclosed its financial details or forecasts.
AJVC, led by Aviral Bhatnagar, is an early-stage investment firm with a portfolio spanning startups such as Alchemic, Bubble Me, Finanjo, Mindcase, Care Dale, HandyPanda, Multibagg AI, Nuyug, Mithila Foods, Jaagruk Bharat, TruFides AI, Chop Finance, Gaadi Mech, and Iztri.

The round takes its total capital raised to $22.5 million.
The startup had previously raised $1.2 million in a pre-seed round led by Pear VC in October 2024 and $6.1 million in a seed round led by Spark Capital in April 2025.

According to Piston, merchants gain access to high-margin commercial fuel volumes and increased in-store sales, while fleet owners get real-time visibility into every gallon purchased, linked to a specific driver and vehicle.
The company claims its payment volume grew 8X year-on-year, while its merchant network expanded 40X, with customer retention at 98%. Piston is now deployed at more than 2,000 stations across 48 states. Its point-of-sale integrations are also certified and live across systems covering more than 95% of US merchant fuel sites.
Piston also plans to expand its real-time controls with two AI-powered products. Its Guard product evaluates each transaction for anomalies and can flag or block suspected fraudulent spending before it is completed. Meanwhile, the Piston Analytics Agent enables fleet owners to analyse spending data and identify patterns without spending hours on manual analysis.

title: The lending bet: why we started with the problem, not the loan
summary:
Lending is where a lot of financial services businesses eventually end up. The reason is fairly obvious. It is a very hard business to build, but if you can pull it off, it can also be a very profitable one. We have seen that repeatedly through history and across markets.
The way we looked at lending at Better Capital was slightly different though. We did not come from a traditional banking or lending background. Our lens was much more consumer tech, product and distribution first.
So instead of starting with, say, we are going to offer personal loans and then figure out how to acquire customers for them, we started with a different question. What is a real problem we can solve for a customer that naturally puts us in front of someone who may eventually need a loan?
That became quite central to how we thought about lending.
The idea was that if you solve an important problem first, you acquire the customer through a genuinely useful experience. By the time the lending opportunity shows up, the customer already knows you, you understand a lot more about them and the context in which they need the money, and you should be in a much better position to serve and underwrite them.
We believed that could create a very interesting flywheel. Solve the problem, build the relationship, understand the customer and then make credit available when it is actually needed.
OTO is a good example of this.
You could describe OTO as a two wheeler financing company, but that misses a large part of how the experience was built. If you were looking to buy a two wheeler, and increasingly an electric two wheeler, OTO helped you discover and understand the options. It also did something that was pretty unusual when it started. With a click, you could schedule a test ride at your home.
So OTO entered the customer’s journey well before the financing decision. You came to explore what you wanted to buy, got a great experience, took a test ride and moved closer to making a purchase. By the time you needed financing, OTO already understood a meaningful part of your buying journey and had built a relationship with you.
The financing then became a natural extension of the experience rather than the starting point.
Khatabook is probably an even cleaner example of this idea.
Khatabook started by solving an extremely simple but important problem for small businesses. It gave merchants a digital ledger to keep track of the money they were owed and the credit they extended to their customers.
Over time, millions of merchants started using Khatabook to run an important part of their business. That relationship created something very valuable. Khatabook understood these businesses, how they operated and increasingly the financial behaviour around them.
Lending could then become a natural extension of that relationship.
Instead of acquiring a small business owner because they clicked on an ad for a loan, you already had a customer using your product to run their business. You had solved something useful for them first. And because you understood the customer better, you had the potential to build a much stronger lending business around that relationship.
Khatabook has done very well with this approach, and I think it captures a lot of what we originally believed about how technology companies could enter lending.
Rupeek approached the opportunity from a completely different direction.
Gold loans have existed forever in India, but the experience of getting one was quite broken. You had to physically go somewhere with your gold and go through a process that could be cumbersome and, for many customers, simply not a great experience.
Rupeek asked if that experience itself could be completely reimagined. They built an at home model and made the entire journey dramatically simpler.
Again, the idea was not just to offer another gold loan. It was to solve the experience around getting a gold loan in a way that nobody had really done at scale. That experience itself became the wedge, and Rupeek went on to build what I think is one of the strongest new brands in gold lending in India.
Jai Kisan takes the same broad idea into rural India.
Farmers, retailers and small rural businesses have very different financial lives from the urban salaried consumer that a lot of traditional fintech was initially built around. Their cash flows are different, their businesses work differently and the context in which they need credit is different.
So if you understand that customer, their business and the ecosystem around them deeply enough, you should be able to build financial products that work much better for them than a generic lending product ever could.
That is what made Jai Kisan interesting to us. The starting point was not simply that rural India needs loans. It was understanding how these customers actually operate and then building credit around that reality.
IppoPay is another version of the same thesis, focused on very small businesses.
For many of these merchants, the starting point is payments and managing the basic financial activity of the business. If you can become a trusted financial partner there, over time you understand the merchant and their business much better.
And once that relationship exists, lending becomes a logical extension. You are not meeting the merchant for the first time when they need money. You already understand something about how their business works and can potentially support them with credit in a much more informed way.
IppoPay has been scaling well in this segment, and I think there is a lot of opportunity ahead as they deepen that financial relationship with these businesses.
So OTO, Khatabook, Rupeek, Jai Kisan and IppoPay look like very different companies.
And that is really the point.
Two wheelers. Small business ledgers. Gold loans. Rural commerce. Payments for micro businesses.
What connects them is not the type of loan.
It is the way they get to the loan.
Start with the problem. Find a way to be useful to the customer before asking them to borrow. Build the product and distribution around that problem. Understand the customer and the context in which they operate. And then, if credit is a natural part of solving that problem, you have an interesting opportunity to build lending around a relationship that already exists.
None of this makes lending easy.
The last five to seven years of digital lending in India have had plenty of ups and downs. Regulation has evolved significantly as the ecosystem has dealt with mis selling, data privacy, aggressive recovery practices and many of the other problems that appeared as digital lending scaled.
Companies across the ecosystem have had to change structures, processes and sometimes large parts of their businesses to adapt. There has been a lot of pain along the way.
But much of that was necessary. The regulatory framework is considerably clearer today, companies understand the boundaries much better, and the ones that have made it through this period have had to build with a lot more discipline around compliance and customer protection.
The first generation of digital lending companies in India has already shown what is possible. But I think there is a lot more to come.
Credit is such a fundamental financial need across consumers, small businesses, farmers, commerce, housing and almost every part of the economy. There will continue to be very large lending businesses built in India.
Our lens on where some of the most interesting ones might come from has remained fairly consistent.
When I look at a new lending company, the first question I find myself asking is not, what loan are you offering?
It is, what problem are you solving before the loan?

 
The fourth of a five-part series by Vaibhav Domkundwar examines the lending thesis behind investments in OTO, Khatabook, Rupeek, Jai Kisan, and IppoPay. The piece explores how these companies started by solving a specific customer problem and built lending as a natural extension of the relationship. The final part will explore another key microtrend and lesson from Better Capital’s investment journey.

Non-institutional investors (NII) led the demand, with their portion subscribed 3.87X. The employee portion was subscribed 2.09X, while the retail portion saw 2.05X subscription. In contrast, the qualified institutional buyers (QIB) portion was subscribed 0.41X on the first day.

It allows customers to rent products on monthly plans instead of purchasing them outright. The company has expanded its rental network across major Indian cities and competes with players such as Furlenco and Cityfurnish.
Rentomojo reported revenue from operations of Rs 387 crore in FY26, up 45.5% from the previous year. Its profit rose 142% year-on-year to Rs 104 crore during the fiscal year.
At the upper end of the IPO price band, the company is seeking a valuation of around $444 million. The fresh issue proceeds will be used towards debt repayment and other corporate purposes.
The IPO is being managed by Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors, Axis Capital and IIFL Capital Services. Rentomojo shares are expected to list on the NSE and BSE on September 17.

summary:
Quick food delivery startup Swish has raised $24 million in a funding round led by Bertelsmann India Investments (BII), with participation from existing investors Accel, Bain Capital Ventures and Hara Global.
Entrackr had exclusively reported the development on Monday.
Founded by Aniket Shah, Ujjwal Sukheja and Saran S., Swish operates a network of neighbourhood kitchens that prepare and deliver fresh food within 10 minutes. The company currently operates across Bengaluru, Gurugram, Noida, Delhi and Ghaziabad.
The company claims its monthly orders have crossed 1 million, with the order volume tripling since March 2026. Its menu has expanded to more than 250 SKUs across over 20 food categories, while lunch and dinner now account for a larger share of orders than snacks and late-night meals.
The fresh capital will be used to expand Swish’s kitchen network, strengthen its supply chain infrastructure and increase capacity. The company plans to enter more cities and is targeting more than 1,000 kitchens over the next five years.
Swish claims over 80% of its orders are delivered within 15 minutes. The startup currently covers around 50 pincodes and plans to expand its footprint as it scales.
Prior to this round, Swish had raised around $54 million, including a $14 million round in March 2025. As per Entrackr estimates, Swish will be valued at around $175 million post money.
Launched in July 2024, Swish reported Rs 4 crore in revenue and a total loss of Rs 19 crore during the eight-month period of FY25. The company is yet to file its FY26 financial results.
The latest round comes as the quick food delivery segment sees growing competition from Blinkit’s Bistro, Zepto Cafe and Swiggy’s Bolt. Swish also operates in the broader online food delivery and cloud kitchen market, where players such as Rebel Foods and Curefoods have established operations.

title: Fleet management platform Carrum Mobility raises $10 Mn in Series B led by Uber
summary:
Carrum Mobility, a B2B fleet management platform, has raised $10 million (approximately Rs 96 crore) in a Series B funding round led by Uber. This is Uber’s second investment in the company, following its $7 million investment in January 2026.
The fresh capital will be used to expand into existing and new geographies, strengthen its technology platform and scale operations, Carrum Mobility said in a press release.
Founded in 2024 by Karan Jain, Carrum Mobility provides fleet management solutions for CNG and electric vehicles. The platform uses technology and data to manage fleet utilisation and driver operations.
Since Uber’s previous investment in January 2026, Carrum Mobility said it has nearly doubled its business, driven by demand for premium mobility services.
The company claims to operate more than 5,000 vehicles across Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Delhi and Kolkata as of September 2026. It has over 18,000 driver partners, while its Chennai operations are expected to go live in September 2026.
Carrum Mobility competes with Uber-backed fleet operator Everest Fleet, which received a $20 million investment from Uber in November 2025. Uber had previously invested $30 million in Everest Fleet in September 2024.
Carrum Mobility said it has been profitable since its first month of operations and has reached an annualised revenue run rate of approximately Rs 400 crore within around two years of starting operations.

title: Bounce returns to scooter rentals with 14K EVs, turns EBITDA profitable in FY26
summary:
Bounce has restarted its scooter rental business with electric two-wheelers manufactured by the company, moving further toward a recurring-revenue model focused on gig and delivery workers.
The Bengaluru-based electric mobility startup is now close to deploying 14,000 scooters on rentals and is expected to reach 20,000 soon, according to people aware of the company’s operations. The rental business is generating an annualised revenue run rate of around $15 million, they added.
The progress comes as Bounce reported Rs 44.05 crore in consolidated operating revenue in FY26. Rental services emerged as its largest revenue stream, contributing Rs 35.78 crore, or around 81% of operating revenue, according to its financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
The company also reported Rs 9.59 crore in consolidated EBITDA during the fiscal year. While the reported EBITDA included some non-cash items, people familiar with the business said Bounce has since reached profitability at the group level. The company recorded a PAT margin of around 19% in July, they added.
Bounce had earlier focused on selling electric scooters directly to consumers. It has now restarted rentals using its own electric vehicles, with Bounce Daily targeting gig and delivery workers who need two-wheelers for work without the upfront cost of buying one.
The rental model gives Bounce a recurring revenue stream while allowing it to use its manufacturing capabilities more directly. Unlike operators that depend on third-party OEMs, Bounce controls the vehicle design, manufacturing, and maintenance cycle, according to people familiar with the company.
This full-stack approach is also central to the company’s economics. Bounce’s own scooters are purpose-built for gig workers, while in-house manufacturing reduces dependence on external OEMs for parts and spares and can help minimise vehicle downtime.
The shift is visible in the company’s FY26 cost structure. As scooter sales reduced, material costs fell significantly, while rental income became the dominant contributor to operating revenue. Bounce’s total expenses stood at around Rs 76 crore during the year.
The reported EBITDA, however, needs some context. Bounce recorded Rs 23.32 crore in other income mainly from the write-back of GST input credit, a non-cash item. It also reported around Rs 11.4 crore in non-cash expenses, including Rs 7 crore related to the FAME subsidy and Rs 4.4 crore related to advances, inventory and receivables.
After adjusting for these items and ESOP costs, the company’s adjusted EBITDA stood at a loss of Rs 1.83 crore in FY26. Its consolidated net loss was Rs 5.48 crore, while cash flow from operating activities remained negative at Rs 6.23 crore.
The latest operating numbers suggest that the rental business has since moved ahead of the FY26 reported base. With close to 14,000 scooters already deployed and a path toward 20,000, the key question is whether Bounce can sustain fleet utilisation and margins as it scales.
For Bounce, the advantage is not simply owning a rental fleet. Its integrated manufacturing and rental model gives it greater control over vehicle availability, maintenance and product design. If the company can maintain high utilisation while keeping acquisition and operating costs under control, rentals could become a more durable business than its earlier consumer sales model.

title: Flipkart starts employee testing of ‘Eat In’ food delivery service in Bengaluru
summary:
Flipkart has started testing its food delivery service Eat In among employees in Bengaluru. The e-commerce major is now moving closer to a market dominated by Zomato and Swiggy.
According to a Moneycontrol report citing sources, the service is expected to be rolled out to all Flipkart employees around September 15 before it becomes available to consumers in Bengaluru.
For now, Eat In will be available within the main Flipkart app. Sources said Flipkart may launch a separate app for the food delivery service at a later stage as it scales the business. After Bengaluru, the company is expected to expand the service to other cities, sources added.
Flipkart’s entry comes amid intensifying competition in India’s food delivery market. Players are adopting different models to appeal to price conscious consumers.
Rapido’s food delivery service Ownly, which follows a zero commission model for restaurants, recently crossed 50,000 daily orders in Bengaluru. Meanwhile, Swiggy’s affordable food delivery offering Toing now matches Zomato in weekly active users, according to CLSA.
Flipkart had confirmed its plans to enter food delivery in July. Flipkart Group CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy said the service would initially be another use case within its ecommerce platform.
The food delivery push comes as Flipkart continues to add new use cases to its platform. The company recently entered the micro drama segment and now offers short form video content within its app. Flipkart also operates in fashion through Myntra, travel through Cleartrip, financial services through super.money and quick commerce through Flipkart Minutes.
The company will now compete with Eternal owned Zomato and Swiggy. Newer offerings such as Rapido’s Ownly and Swiggy’s Toing are also seeking to gain share through alternative pricing and value focused models.

title: PhonePe, Visa launch cardless payment solutions for consumers and merchants
summary:
Fintech company PhonePe has partnered with Visa to launch three payment solutions, Tap to Pay, Cross Border Scan to Pay and Smart Accept, aimed at enabling cardless payments for consumers and merchants.
The solutions were unveiled at the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026. PhonePe said the partnership makes it the first app in India to introduce Cross Border Scan to Pay for international transactions.
Under Tap to Pay, Android users can tokenise their Visa cards on PhonePe and make contactless payments at point of sale machines. The feature will be rolled out in phases, starting September 9, 2026.
Cross Border Scan to Pay will allow users to scan Visa supported QR codes across 14 international markets, including Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Japan, China and South Korea. The feature is expected to be rolled out to users soon.
The partnership also builds on Visa's online device tokenisation feature, which was introduced on PhonePe in February 2025. It enables users to save their Visa cards on the platform and use tokenised card credentials for online transactions across participating ecommerce merchants.
Meanwhile, Smart Accept will enable small merchants to accept card payments directly through their smartphones without requiring a separate point of sale machine. Customers can pay by tapping physical cards or tokenised mobile wallets against the merchant's device.
Smart Accept will also be integrated with PhonePe's existing QR dashboard, allowing merchants to manage card payments along with their other transactions.
PhonePe said the initiative brings together Visa's tokenisation and payment capabilities with its consumer and merchant network to expand cardless payment options in India and for Indians travelling abroad. 
As of July 2026, PhonePe said it had more than 71.5 crore registered users and a digital payments acceptance network spanning over 5 crore merchants.

title: Rentomojo raises Rs 376 Cr from anchor investors ahead of IPO
summary:
Furniture and appliance rental platform Rentomojo has secured Rs 376.07 crore from anchor investors ahead of the opening of its initial public offering (IPO).
Rentomojo’s IPO opens for subscription today, September 9, and will close on September 11.
The Bengaluru-based company allotted 93.08 lakh equity shares to anchor investors at Rs 404 apiece, the upper end of its IPO price band. At this price, Rentomojo will command a valuation of around Rs 4,200 crore.
The anchor round saw participation from domestic mutual funds, insurance companies, and pension funds. Key participants included Kotak ELSS Tax Saver Fund, ICICI Prudential Quality Fund, Goldman Sachs India Equity Portfolio, BlackRock Global Funds - India Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund, Mirae Asset Great Consumer Fund, Bandhan Innovation Fund, HSBC Mutual Fund, Invesco India, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund and JM Financial Mutual Fund.
Domestic mutual funds received 60,41,249 shares, accounting for 64.90% of the anchor allocation, through 30 schemes across 16 mutual funds, for a total of Rs 244.07 crore. The allocation to life insurance companies and pension funds stood at 12.62 lakh shares, or 13.56% of the anchor portion, worth Rs 51 crore. 
According to its RHP, Rentomojo plans to raise Rs 1,255.6 crore through the IPO, comprising a fresh issue of Rs 150 crore and an OFS of 2.73 crore shares worth Rs 1,105.6 crore.
The OFS includes shares sold by existing investors Accel India, Edelweiss, Chiratae Ventures, ValueQuest, Madison India and GMO, along with founder Geetansh Bamania. 
Motilal Oswal, Axis Capital and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers.
Earlier, Entrackr reported that several early Rentomojo investors are set to generate significant returns through the IPO, with some early backers expected to clock up to 152X returns on their OFS.
The company's revenue from operations rose 45.5% year-on-year to Rs 387 crore in FY26, while profit after tax jumped 142% to Rs 104.2 crore from Rs 43.1 crore in FY25.

title: Exclusive: Fashion brand Theater raises Series A at Rs 400 Cr valuation
summary:
Digital-first fashion brand Theater has raised Rs 56.25 crore (around $6 million) in Series A funding as it builds on strong growth over the past two fiscal years. The round was led by Niveshaay, with participation from FirstPort Capital, Skagen Ventures and other investors.
In September 2024, the company had raised $1.5 million in a pre-Series A round led by Prath Ventures.
The board at Theater approved the issuance of 2,145 Series A CCPS at an issue price of Rs 2,62,224 per share to raise the aforementioned amount, according to its regulatory filings.
Niveshaay led the round with an investment of Rs 37 crore, followed by FirstPort Capital with Rs 12.81 crore and Skagen Ventures with Rs 3.36 crore. Saket Agarwal, Vishal Julka, and IPV International also participated in the round.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, the company’s valuation stood at around Rs 402 crore ($43 million) post-money, a 4.5X increase from its previous valuation of Rs 90 crore. The fresh capital will be used to expand the business, meet working capital needs, strengthen the balance sheet and support future growth.
Founded by Sarthak Aggarwa, Karan Jain, Vikram Jain, and Shruti Agarwal, Theater is a digital-first fashion and lifestyle brand offering shoes, bags, stockings, socks, perfumes, and other accessories for men and women.
After allotment of this round, Eternal Emerging Enterprises Fund remains the largest institutional shareholder with a 9.71%, followed by Niveshaay with 9.20%, FirstPort Capital with 3.19%, and Vishal Julka with 2.54%.
Among the co-founders, Sarthak Aggarwal holds a 20.63% stake, while Karan Jain and Vikram Jain own 16.39% each. Shruti Aggarwal holds a 12.16% stake in the five-year-old company.
A Moneycontrol report had earlier said that Theater XYZ was in talks to raise $4-5 million in a funding round led by Niveshaay.
Theater is yet to file its FY26 results, but the 4.5X jump in valuation alongside its latest fundraise suggests investors have seen enough progress to back the brand at a much higher level. After 2.37X revenue growth to Rs 33.35 crore in FY25, the FY26 numbers will show whether Theater has sustained that momentum.
With its investment in Theater, Niveshaay is actively expanding its focus on the D2C space. The firm has recently backed travel and lifestyle brand Mokobara and innerwear brand XYXX, while its earlier investments include beauty brands Naturis Cosmetics and Innovist.

title: Deep-tech cybersecurity company QNu Labs raises Rs 200 Cr in Series A1 round
summary:
Deep-tech cybersecurity company QNu Labs has raised Rs 200 crore in a Series A1 funding round co-led by the National Quantum Mission (NQM) and Speciale Invest, with participation from Sony Innovation Fund, Gaja Capital and Artha Ventures. The round takes QNu Labs’ total capital raised to Rs 375 crore.
The Bengaluru-based startup was incubated at IIT Madras. It previously raised Rs 60 crore ($7 million) in a Series A round led by the National Quantum Mission in April last year and $6.5 million in a pre-Series A1 round led by Ashish Kacholia of Lucky Investments in December 2023.
The fresh funds will be used to accelerate R&D, strengthen its technology capabilities, and scale sales and go-to-market operations across India and international markets, QNu Labs said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2016 by Srinivasa Rao Aluri and Sunil Gupta, QNu Labs offers quantum-safe infrastructure and platform solutions that enable clients to adopt quantum-safe security technologies without disrupting existing business operations.
QNu Labs plans to contribute to an approved project funded under the RDI programme to build the technology backbone for India’s Quantum Secure and Sensing Networks (IQSN). It also plans to expand its quantum-safe technology stack into quantum sensing and AI, increase deployments across critical sectors, and build capabilities to address demand for quantum-safe migration globally.
QNu Labs said its patented, certified and military-grade products and solutions are deployed by clients globally to secure critical infrastructure. The company plans to expand these deployments as demand for quantum-safe security solutions grows.
Startups in this space are developing infrastructure and platform layers based on technologies such as Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), Quantum Random Number Generation (QRNG), Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) and cryptographic key management. These technologies allow organisations to upgrade their security architecture while maintaining existing systems.
Startups working across quantum technologies include QpiAI, Dimira Technologies, PRENISHQ, QuPrayog, Quanastra and Quan2D Technologies.

title: The consumer fintech bet: why India was never one market
summary:
Ajinkya Kulkarni showed up at our office in Pune one day with a fairly simple idea. He wanted to build a liquid fixed income product that could give consumers an attractive return, around 12% at the time.
I remember thinking this was interesting because I had been wondering if there was an opportunity to build something like a Yieldstreet for India. The two ideas matched almost immediately, so we started talking.
That led to a lot of brainstorming around fixed income, how consumers in India thought about it, what was missing, and how much easier the whole experience could be made. We started calling the vision the Passive Income App of India, and that was really the beginning of what eventually became Wint Wealth.
A lot has changed since then, both in the company and in the market, but Wint has really been one of the torchbearers of making fixed income accessible to Indian consumers. They built the product, educated consumers at scale and created what I think is one of the best fixed income experiences in India.
But the Wint story is also part of a much broader way we have thought about consumer financial services at Better.
When people talk about the Indian consumer, there is often a tendency to talk about hundreds of millions of users as if they are one large market. We have never really looked at it that way.
India is almost the opposite.
It is a collection of a very large number of consumer segments, each potentially tens of millions of people, that can be quite different from one another. What work they do, how much they earn, how predictable that income is, what they aspire to, how they save, how they invest, and what kind of financial products make sense to them can all be completely different.
A gig worker is a very different financial services customer from a young salaried professional. That person is different again from an NRI, a crypto investor, a mass affluent investor or an ultra HNI.
And our view was that if these users are so different, why should the financial experience built for each of them look the same?
We believed there was an opportunity to build a dramatically better, almost 10x experience for each of these segments. And quite often, we believed these would need to be different companies altogether.
The founder DNA required to understand one of these consumers deeply can be very different from another. The product, distribution, trust, partnerships and the way you think about the customer can all be different. We never really believed that you could build one generic financial services company and simply keep adding ten products for ten very different segments underneath it.
That thinking informed a lot of our consumer fintech investing.
Wint was one expression of it. Fixed income had historically been relatively cumbersome for consumers to discover and invest in. Wint essentially took that experience and rebuilt it around what a modern consumer would want.
Gullak came from another direction altogether. Gold is already deeply understood and trusted in India. The opportunity was to make saving in gold incredibly simple and build a modern experience around something Indians have been doing forever. It has been a phenomenal journey watching the team build the product, the brand and partnerships across the offline jewellery ecosystem, and I think they are still scratching the surface of what is possible.
Mudrex was another early investment for us. Crypto was clearly going to attract a completely different kind of investor, but investing in it in India could be confusing and intimidating. Mudrex built one of the most trusted ways for Indian users to invest in crypto, with compliance at the center of how they approached the market. Watching the team build out Mudrex over the years has been another incredible journey.
Then there is SBNRI, which went after another massive segment altogether.
There are millions of Indians living around the world who want to invest back into India. But the experience can involve banking, KYC, taxation, repatriation, documentation and a whole set of hoops that are very specific to an NRI.
SBNRI essentially asked: why does this have to be so cumbersome?
They were one of the earliest companies to focus deeply on the NRI investing experience and built much of the product and underlying workflow required to make it dramatically more streamlined. They have built a tremendous brand in the segment, and I think they are still just getting started.
So if you zoom out, Wint, Gullak, Mudrex and SBNRI look like very different companies.
And that is exactly the point.
They are all expressions of the same underlying idea: take a particular segment of consumers, understand what is broken or unnecessarily difficult about their financial experience, and build something dramatically better specifically for them.
For a while, we felt we had built a pretty interesting portfolio around this idea. Different founders going after different parts of financial services, each trying to create a much better experience for a particular kind of customer.
And then AI showed up.
That made us look at the same thesis again.
Our existing companies are obviously going to use AI to make their products easier and better. But we also started wondering whether AI makes it possible to build an entirely new financial experience for a segment whose relationship with money itself is quite different.
Gen Z was an obvious place to look.
How a 22 or 25 year old thinks about earning, spending, saving, travel, experiences, work and eventually investing can be quite different from the way previous generations were taught to think about personal finance. Yet most financial products still start from a fairly traditional framework and essentially ask the user to adapt to it.
We felt AI could change that.
That is what led us to our latest investment in this thesis, Smooth Money.
The way I think about Smooth is as a personal financial companion for Gen Z. It should understand your life, your behaviour and what you are trying to do with your money.
It is not there to tell you that you should not have had that extra coffee because it interferes with your SIP goal. That is not how people actually want to live.
Instead, it understands how you already live and helps you make better decisions around that. It can help create savings buckets, think through goals, understand spending and increasingly become something you can simply have a conversation with about your money.
Think of it as every Gen Z having their own personalized financial advisor.
We are still very early in that journey, but I am extremely excited about what Smooth can become.
In some ways, Smooth is simply the latest version of the same thesis we started with years ago.
There is no single Indian financial services consumer.
There are many Indias sitting inside India, with different incomes, professions, behaviours, aspirations and relationships with money. And technology keeps making it possible to build a dramatically better financial experience for each of them.
We are going from a relatively small number of rigid, cumbersome, one size fits all financial products to a world where founders can build very specific experiences for very specific consumers.
AI should take that personalization much further.
So when I look at Wint, Gullak, Mudrex, SBNRI, Smooth and several of the other companies we have backed around this idea, I do not think this journey is anywhere close to done.
If anything, I think we are still at the beginning of moving from financial products built for everyone to financial experiences built for you.
The third of a five-part series by Vaibhav Domkundwar explores the consumer fintech thesis behind investments in Wint Wealth, Gullak, Mudrex, SBNRI, and Smooth Money. The piece argues that India is not a single consumer market, with different segments requiring distinct financial products and experiences. The next two parts will explore other microtrends and lessons.

summary:
Alco-bev startup Marmalade has raised Rs 6 crore in a seed funding round from a clutch of investors, including Ashok Chokalingam, Robert Sellares, Ishank Gupta, and HomeLane founders Srikanth Iyer and Tanuj Choudhry.
The proceeds will be deployed towards expanding distribution, brand-building initiatives, and strengthening sales and operational capabilities, Marmalade said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2025 by Udit Mediratta and Surojit Bhattacharya, Marmalade is a new-age drinks company building spirits for the next generation of Indian consumers. The company creates easy-drinking, flavour-forward alcoholic beverages aimed at making drinking more enjoyable, approachable, and relevant to today's consumers.
Marmalade's flagship brand, Brightside, is an Indian craft whiskey developed in partnership with Amrut Distilleries and master blender Ashok Chokalingam. The brand aims to offer a different way for a new generation to discover and experience whiskey through its product, branding, and category-focused innovations.
The Delhi-based startup plans to expand into Mumbai and the broader Maharashtra market. The company claims it is on track to reach an annualised revenue run rate (ARR) of Rs 5 crore in September 2026 and is targeting Rs 15 crore in ARR by December 2026. This would represent threefold growth in less than four months across two cities.
According to Marmalade, Brightside Craft Whiskey combines fine malts and grain spirits with a distinctive blend of botanicals to create a smoother and more approachable drinking experience, without the harsh burn, bitterness, and strong aftertaste. Brightside has also incorporated packaging innovations aimed at making the drinking experience more engaging.
Brightside Craft Whiskey is priced at Rs 1,750 for a 750 ml bottle in Maharashtra. The brand aims to occupy a price segment between Rs 1,500 and Rs 2,200, which it describes as having limited offerings.
India's alcobev startups are experimenting with craft whisky, gin, agave spirits, and liqueurs while placing greater emphasis on contemporary branding, smoother profiles, locally sourced ingredients, and premium-but-approachable pricing.
Recently, Feline Spirits raised Rs 5.2 crore in a pre-Series A round led by Inflection Point Ventures. Raincheck Earth Co., the maker of Cherrapunji Craft Gin, raised $1.2 million from Japanese investors and the AngelList India Syndicate to scale its craft-gin business. Nuvola Spirits, which makes Mikiamo Limoncello, secured Rs 1.57 crore in pre-Series A funding.

TPG-backed NewQuest Asia Fund IV has offloaded another 1.36% stake in logistics startup Shadowfax for around Rs 200 crore through a bulk deal on the BSE.
According to exchange data, NewQuest sold 80 lakh shares at Rs 250.03 apiece, while OxBow Master Fund bought 47.85 lakh shares at Rs 250 each, worth around Rs 119.6 crore.
The transaction follows a similar deal in August, when NewQuest sold 1.25 crore Shadowfax shares at Rs 240.46 apiece for around Rs 300.6 crore. OxBow Master Fund had bought 69.32 lakh shares at Rs 240.25 apiece in that transaction worth Rs 166.5 crore.
As of June 2026, NewQuest held an 11.53% stake in Shadowfax. Across the two transactions, it has sold around 2.05 crore shares worth over Rs 500 crore, while Oxbow acquired a 2% stake in the company.
The latest deal comes as Shadowfax continues to see secondary-market activity following its public listing.
In Q1 FY27, Shadowfax recorded a 65% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 1,358 crore. Its profit also surged more than eightfold to Rs 65 crore during the quarter.
At the end of Tuesday’s trading session, Shadowfax's share price closed at around Rs 249.8 on BSE, valuing the company at Rs 14,656 crore (approximately $1.54 billion).

summary:
Kuku Technologies, the parent company of Kuku FM and Kuku TV, is building a 1,000-member AI-led content production unit as it looks to scale its microdrama business globally, according to people familiar with the matter. 
The company has already hired nearly 200 people for the Mumbai-based unit and plans to expand the team to around 1,000 by the end of the current financial year, the sources said. 
The hiring comes as Kuku has confidentially filed draft IPO papers with market regulator SEBI for a public issue of up to Rs 3,500 crore. The company is targeting a valuation of around $1.8 billion through the IPO.
Kuku is bringing writers, filmmakers and engineers into the new AI-native unit. Writers will develop stories and dialogues, filmmakers will focus on visual direction, while engineers will build AI systems for areas such as narrative continuity across long-running series.
Kuku expects AI to cut microdrama production costs to 30-50% of China’s, with production costing under $100 per minute versus over $150 in China, sources said. AI-led production can also help one person produce around 20 minutes of usable video a day, compared with about a minute through traditional shoots. 
Kuku declined to comment when contacted.
Founded in 2018 by IIT alumni Lal Chand Bisu, Vinod Kumar, and Vikas Goyal, Kuku operates vernacular audio platform Kuku FM, short-video app Kuku TV, and edutainment platform Guru. Across its platforms, Kuku claims to have over 10 million active paying subscribers, 400 million app downloads, and a content library of more than 60,000 hours spanning several Indian languages. 
The company has raised over $150 million from investors including Fundamentum Partnership, Krafton, Vertex Ventures, Granite Asia, IFC, Paramark Ventures, India Quotient, and 3one4 Capital. Former Indian cricket captain MS Dhoni is also among its backers.
According to sources, Kuku's revenue grew nearly sevenfold to more than Rs 1,400 crore in FY26 from Rs 240 crore in the fiscal year ending March 2025.

title: Circolife raises $4.5 Mn in pre-Series A round led by Bharat Jaisinghani
summary:
Cooling-as-a-Service (CaaS) platform Circolife has raised $4.5 million (around Rs 40.45 crore) in a pre-Series A funding round led by Bharat Jaisinghani, joint managing director of Polycab India. The round also saw participation from a group of individual, fund and family-office investors, including Nitish Mittersain, Intelliquity Ventures, Sumit Jalan, Siddharth Ladsariya, Anand Ladsariya, Anant Goenka, Sky Impact Capital, Rohit Dev, and family offices S N Damani and Vyom Wealth.
The fresh funds will be used to expand its fleet and geographic footprint, scale its in-house installation and service capabilities, and advance its AI-augmented IoT predictive-maintenance and digital twin platform, Circolife said in a press release.
Founded in 2023 by Abhishek Murarka, Tushar Patil and Devanshu Mishra, Circolife owns, installs and services the air-conditioning units it deploys throughout their working life. The startup uses embedded IoT sensors and predictive maintenance to monitor the fleet and refurbishes and redeploys units at the end of their life cycle.
The Thane-based startup said it currently operates across five Indian cities, serving small businesses and enterprise customers across restaurants, hotels, gyms, salons, co-living operators and corporate offices through a subscription-based model for cooling.
Under its subscription model, Circolife installs and maintains the air-conditioning units while customers pay a monthly fee. The company said its units are designed for energy efficiency, while its ownership of the equipment over the contract period allows it to monitor and maintain their performance.
According to Circolife, its units are connected devices equipped with sensors that track temperature, power consumption and gas pressure in real time. This data feeds into a predictive-maintenance system designed to identify potential equipment failures before they result in breakdowns. The startup is also using AI and additional sensors to build digital twins of its deployed devices.
Circolife plans to increase its subscription base fourfold and reach 40,000 units within the next 24 months.
Cooling-as-a-Service is gaining traction within India’s climate-tech and energy-efficiency startup ecosystem, allowing businesses to access air-conditioning and cooling infrastructure without making the upfront capital investment.
Smart Joules, which operates a CaaS model through its JouleCool platform, raised $10 million in Series B funding in December last year from SVL SME Neev II Fund, Waaree Renewable Technologies and Spectrum Impact. The company is using the capital to expand its cooling and energy-efficiency operations across manufacturing, building automation and district cooling.
Other startups exploring the broader cooling-as-a-service and thermal-management space include Tan90, which has raised funding for its thermal-energy-storage solutions and launched a CaaS model for cold-chain businesses.

summary:
India’s broking industry added around 5.12 lakh net active clients in August. Groww accounted for nearly 44% of these additions. The market leader added 2.23 lakh active clients during the month, while Sahi recorded the fastest growth among the top 20 brokers.
Groww’s active client base rose from 1.31 crore in July to 1.33 crore in August. Its market share increased from 28.88% to 29.04%.
Zerodha remained the second-largest broker with 67.97 lakh active clients, after a 34,501 clients addition. Angel One retained the third position with 67.19 lakh clients, following an addition of 84,636 users. Their market shares stood at 14.79% and 14.62%, respectively.

Among the top five, ICICI Securities added 23,385 active clients, taking its total to 21.56 lakh, with a 1.10% monthly rise. Upstox added 3,749 users to reach 18.65 lakh, with a 0.20% monthly rise. Their market shares stood at 4.69% and 4.06%, respectively.
Kotak Securities and HDFC Securities ranked sixth and seventh with 13.92 lakh and 13.51 lakh active clients, respectively. Kotak added 9,440 users, while HDFC Securities added 16,198 clients.

D2C athleisure brand BlissClub recently raised Rs 160 crore ($16.8 million) in a Series B round led by Singularity AMC, with Meesho CEO Vidit Aatrey and existing investors Elevation Capital and Eight Roads Ventures also participating. The funding comes amid continued investor interest in India’s D2C apparel and sportswear space.
The fresh capital has pushed BlissClub’s valuation up 62% from its previous round, while the founders’ combined stake has fallen below 40%. Entrackr examined the company’s regulatory filings to decode the latest funding round, cap table, and post-money valuation.
According to the company’s regulatory filings accessed from the Registrar of Companies (RoC), BlissClub’s board approved the issuance of 69,247 Series B compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 24,503.3 per share to raise Rs 160 crore.
Singularity AMC emerged as the largest investor in the round with an investment of Rs 70 crore, followed by Vidit Aatrey with Rs 50 crore. Existing investors Elevation Capital and Eight Roads Ventures invested Rs 24.66 crore and Rs 15.33 crore, respectively.
According to the company, the fresh capital will be used to expand into new categories, scale its offline retail presence, strengthen product development, and hire talent to support its next phase of growth.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, BlissClub’s valuation surged 62% to around Rs 860 crore (approximately $91 million) following the Series B round, from Rs 532 crore during its Series A round.
Following the latest allotment, Elevation Capital holds a 22.19% stake in the company, followed by Eight Roads Ventures at 14.24%. Singularity AMC, which led the Series B round, holds an 8.14% stake, while Vidit Aatrey owns 6.94%. Co-founder Minu Margeret remains the largest shareholder with a 37.03% stake.


Founded in 2020 by Minu Margeret, BlissClub is a D2C athleisure brand that started with technical activewear for Indian women and has expanded into an omnichannel business with over 40 stores and a recently launched menswear line. Its portfolio spans leggings, tops, outerwear and accessories, sold through its website, marketplaces and retail stores.
BlissClub has yet to file its annual financial report for FY26. In FY25, its operating revenue grew 51.5% to Rs 131.58 crore from Rs 86.88 crore in FY24, while its net loss declined 54.1% to Rs 20.16 crore from Rs 43.92 crore during the same period.

title: The fintech infrastructure bet: why the real opportunity was underneath
summary:
My first job out of Berkeley was in enterprise integration, where we connected complex systems like ERP and supply chain platforms, within and across companies, to ultimately deliver a smoother end user experience.
That was where I first understood and appreciated both the importance and, in some ways, the beauty of infrastructure. The end user rarely sees it, but the quality of the experience depends enormously on what sits underneath.
Fast forward to our fintech investing at Better Capital. Soon after developing our neobanking thesis, it became very clear to us that there was an infrastructure layer that was largely independent of the end user experience, but absolutely necessary to enable it.
If India was going to build a new generation of financial services for hundreds of millions of smartphone connected users, someone had to solve the complexity underneath: how fintechs connect with banks, how products get issued and managed, how regulatory requirements are handled, how money moves, and how all of these systems work together reliably.
That led us quite naturally into fintech infrastructure investing.
We started asking a simple question: what is the underlying infrastructure required for all these new financial experiences to exist?
Because whether it was neobanking, new age credit cards, app based lending, investing, wealth management, or many of the experiences that followed, there was almost always a sophisticated infrastructure layer underneath making the product possible.
That thesis has played out quite well.
M2P was one of our earliest investments in the space. It has gone on to power some of the largest fintech experiences in India, expand into multiple markets globally, and continue scaling significantly.
Upswing is another example. It is building the infrastructure behind some of the fastest growing investment and wealth fintechs, enabling products such as fixed deposits, bonds, and other investment experiences to be embedded seamlessly into consumer platforms.
Hyperface has done some remarkable work in cards, building infrastructure that allows brands and financial institutions to launch and operate deeply integrated credit card experiences in a way that was much harder to do earlier.
And these are just a few examples. We have invested in several companies across the financial infrastructure stack over the years.
What the last six or seven years have reinforced for us is that in financial services, some of the most important companies may sit one layer below the consumer experience. The more regulated and operationally complex the product, the more valuable that infrastructure becomes. And perhaps most importantly, we have seen that infrastructure built for the complexity and scale of India can increasingly travel well beyond India.
What continues to excite me is that I don’t think this thesis is anywhere close to being played out.
As financial services become more digital, more embedded, more personalized, and increasingly powered by software and AI, the infrastructure underneath them will become even more important. New consumer experiences will require new infrastructure, and new infrastructure will, in turn, make entirely new experiences possible.
Over the last six or seven years, we have seen the beginnings of that in India. I believe some very large financial infrastructure companies will be built here, and several of them should have the opportunity to power financial experiences well beyond India as well.
That remains one of the areas I am most excited about.
*The second of a five-part series by Vaibhav Domkundwar explores the fintech infrastructure layer powering new financial experiences. Investments in M2P, Upswing, and Hyperface reinforced the thesis that the real opportunity often lies underneath the consumer-facing product. The next three parts will explore other microtrends and lessons.

summary:
Logistics and ecommerce enablement platform Shiprocket is showing signs of moving closer to profitability in its first quarterly results after going public.
The company’s consolidated net loss narrowed 24% year-on-year to Rs 13.7 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 18 crore in the same quarter last year.
Shiprocket’s revenue from operations also rose 33.8% to Rs 592 crore from Rs 442 crore in Q1 FY26, according to the unaudited results filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
According to the investor presentation, the company processed 216 million transactions, with a GMV of Rs 34,662 crore and 2.24 lakh active merchants during Q1 FY27.
Its core business revenue grew 22% year-on-year to Rs 412 crore, while its other emerging businesses saw a 70% growth to Rs 180 crore during the quarter.
On the cost side, the cost of merchant solutions was the largest expenditure at Rs 441 crore, while employee benefits stood at Rs 106 crore. Overall, its total expenditure increased to Rs 619 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 474 crore a year earlier.
Meanwhile, Shiprocket’s adjusted EBITDA was positive at Rs 8.9 crore during the quarter, improved from Rs 1 crore in the year-ago period. The company said it remained adjusted EBITDA positive throughout the quarter.
The results come soon after Shiprocket’s stock market debut, making the June quarter an important first test for the company as a listed entity.
The company was trading at Rs 138.49 as of 10:48 AM, giving it a total market capitalisation of Rs 10,076 crore ($1.04 billion).

title: W Health Ventures closes Fund II at Rs 700 Cr
summary:
Healthcare-focused venture firm W Health Ventures (WHV) has closed its second fund at Rs 700 crore, oversubscribing its initial target of Rs 630 crore. 
The fund plans to build 8–10 healthcare companies from the pre-idea stage to category leaders over the next four years.
W Health follows a company-creation model, where its in-house team of physicians, operators and technologists identifies gaps in healthcare delivery and spends 12–18 months evaluating and de-risking an opportunity before bringing in a founding team.
The firm plans to write Rs 30–50 crore cheques and build 2–3 companies every year across India and the US-India corridor.
Fund II has already launched two companies. Everhope Oncology, built with Narayana Health, is focused on coordinated, patient-centric cancer care, while Everbright Health is developing treatments for treatment-resistant depression in the US.
According to W Health Ventures, its portfolio companies have reached 25 million patients to date. The firm said Fund II will focus on solving large, underserved healthcare problems where first-mover solutions can create population-scale impact.
Founded in 2020, W Health Ventures has built companies including Elevate Now, Nivaan, Hoola Health and Everhope Oncology, with offices across Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi and Boston.

Fifteen startups developing technologies across sensors, flow control, spectroscopy, optics and photonics, quantum technology, deposition technology, lab-grown diamonds for semiconductor applications, and automation showcased their innovations at the inaugural HORIBA Innovation Connect in New Delhi.
Selected from nearly 100 registrations received from across India, the startups presented their technologies to an expert jury and engaged with HORIBA’s technical and leadership teams on their potential for further development and application.

title: Udaan to acquire Swiggy-owned Lynk Logistics for Rs 500 Cr
summary:
Foodtech and quick commerce platform Swiggy has agreed to sell its retail distribution business Lynk Logistics to eB2B platform Udaan for Rs 500 crore, in a deal that will expand Udaan’s presence across key consumption markets.
As part of the transaction, Swiggy will receive approximately 2.8% stake in Udaan through preference equity shares issued by Trustroot Internet Pvt Ltd, the parent entity of Udaan. Swiggy will also invest Rs 75 crore in primary equity in Udaan for an additional 0.4% stake.
The transaction comes as Udaan continues to improve its financial performance. Over the 10 quarters from Q4 CY23 to Q1 CY26, its revenue grew at a CAGR of around 25%, while its contribution margin improved by nearly 500 bps and EBITDA burn declined by around 70%. Its private labels now account for 15–25% of Staples sales across operating cities, while Bengaluru, its largest market, has turned EBITDA profitable.
The acquisition will add Lynk’s distribution capabilities, brand relationships and retail network to Udaan’s platform. Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Kolkata together contribute around 75% of Lynk’s revenue. The deal will also help Udaan connect leading consumer brands with a wider network of retailers.
Lynk directly or indirectly competes with the likes of Udaan, 1K Kirana Bazaar, Jumbotail, ElasticRun and several other eB2B and retail distribution platforms. These companies serve retailers through technology-led distribution, procurement and supply chain networks, making the acquisition relevant to Udaan’s competitive position in India’s fragmented retail distribution market.
Swiggy had acquired Lynk in July 2023 through a share swap deal, marking its entry into India’s retail B2B distribution market. The transaction value was not disclosed at the time. Lynk, founded in 2015, had a network of more than 100,000 retail stores across eight cities and worked with leading FMCG brands as an authorised distributor.
The latest transaction also follows Udaan’s $160 million recapitalisation, which comprised fresh equity, new debt and debt-to-equity conversion from Lightspeed Venture Partners, M&G Investments and Moonstone Capital. The exercise included around $45 million in private credit financing from a leading global investment management firm and strengthened Udaan’s balance sheet for its next phase of growth.
Swiggy CFO Rahul Bothra said the deal combines Lynk’s capabilities with Udaan’s scale and technology-led platform, while Udaan cofounder and CEO Vaibhav Gupta said the acquisition strengthens the company’s business and expands its presence across important consumption markets.

title: The neobank bet: what backing digital banks in India actually taught us
summary:
With GFF around the corner, I wanted to reflect on what we have actually learned from our fintech portfolio, especially since fintech was the very first area we focused on when we started the fund.
A core part of how we work at Better has been to identify a microtrend early, build conviction in it, and then back multiple companies around that microtrend before it becomes obvious to everyone else. It has served us well over the years.
The very first microtrend we started with was neobanks. In 2018/19 in India, it wasn't really a term yet. My conviction came partly from a vivid memory of a company called Simple from the late 2000s, whose vision was to build a modern digital bank for small businesses. As a small startup founder myself back then, that was something I related to deeply.
By 2018/19 it felt like the ingredients were finally in place in India. A smartphone-first, data-connected, UPI-led population was ready for a genuinely modern banking experience. A number of teams started building around this time and we made several investments: a neobank for Gen Z, one for NRIs, one for SMBs, and a few more.
Soon there was broader conviction in the market and many companies got funded around the same idea. The next several years were about watching them all build and navigate a hard set of constraints.
The hardest one was structural. You cannot easily get a banking license in India, and that single constraint shaped everything. Without a license, delivering a true full-stack customer experience was very hard. Companies had to depend on bank partnerships, and those dependencies caused delays across product, launches and the ability to control the core experience. Compliance and infrastructure constraints added more friction. Consumer and business adoption was genuinely strong, but the path to the fuller vision kept hitting the same ceiling.
Slice was the one that broke through it. By acquiring a bank and becoming a full-stack neobank, it unlocked the vision many of us had held on to for years. Today, Slice is one of the top credit card issuers in the country within about a year of going full-stack, ahead of many large banks, and posted a PAT of around ₹46 crore in Q1FY27.
And Slice is not the only story here. Several others from this cohort are still very much in play, and they have delivered genuinely incredible improvements in customer experience along the way. I am excited to see how they navigate the next chapter and unlock more of the vision we all started with.
This is exactly why we invest the way we do. Get the microtrend right, back multiple shots at it early, and stay long enough for the category to be redefined. Neobanks were our first real proof of that.
 
*This is the first of a five-part series by Vaibhav Domkundwar on the microtrends that have shaped his investment journey. Neobanks were the starting point, and the experience reinforced a simple thesis: identify a shift early, back the right founders, and stay patient as a category evolves. The next three parts will explore the other microtrends and the lessons they offered.

title: Exclusive: DaMENSCH raises fresh funding at flat valuation of Rs 600 Cr
summary:
DaMENSCH has raised fresh capital from existing backer A91 Partners and new investor Tancom Electronics, but the latest round has not moved its valuation. The flat pricing comes as the direct to consumer men’s apparel market enters a more competitive phase, with brands now under pressure to turn topline growth into profitability.
In May 2024, the company had raised Rs 21.62 crore (approximately $2.5 million) in its extended Series B round from existing investors.
The board at DaMENSCH has approved the allotment of 887 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 1,69,052 per share to raise Rs 15 crore from A91 Partners, according to the company’s regulatory filing accessed through the Registrar of Companies.
Separately, the company issued 168 CCPS at an issue price of Rs 1,42,692 per share to raise Rs 2.40 crore from Tancom Electronics. Together, the two tranches helped DaMENSCH raise Rs 17.40 crore in this round.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, DaMENSCH’s valuation is flat to Rs 600 crore ($63.5 million at current exchange rate) from its previous valuation of $70-75 million or Rs 582 crore . 
The company plans to use the fresh capital to meet its business requirements and support its growth, as per filings.
Founded in 2018 by Anurag Saboo and Gaurav Pushkar, DaMENSCH is a D2C men’s fashion and lifestyle brand that offers innerwear, casualwear, and everyday apparel products via its own platform and marketplaces.
DaMENSCH has raised over $28 million to date, including its $16.6 million Series B round led by A91 Partners in February 2022.
A91 Partners remains the largest shareholder in the company with a 22.45% stake, followed by Matrix with 12.76%. Saama Capital and Whiteboard Capital hold 11.14% and 9.61%, respectively. The company’s co-founders, Gaurav Pushkar and Anurag Saboo, hold 10.87% each.


DaMENSCH is yet to file its FY26 results, but its FY25 performance shows how competition is shaping up in D2C men’s apparel. Its revenue grew 34% to Rs 118 crore, while XYXX scaled 46% to Rs 187 crore and narrowed its loss to Rs 25.5 crore. Bummer remained smaller, with revenue up 22% to Rs 11 crore, but losses doubled. 
The numbers point to a market where brands are scaling, but the gap is emerging in how efficiently they convert growth into profitability. As competition intensifies, scale, repeat purchases and distribution economics will become increasingly important for these firms.

title: Voice AI startup Navana.ai raises Rs 40 Cr led by Ronnie Screwvala

The company plans to deploy the fresh capital to expand its Voice AI deployments among BFSI enterprises, strengthen its speech models for Indian languages and dialects, and develop its AI Contact Centre and automated evaluation platform.
Founded by brothers Raoul and Jai Nanavati, Navana.ai provides voice AI solutions to regulated enterprises, with a focus on data privacy and compliance through on-premise deployments. The startup claims to have processed more than 100 million voice AI minutes for BFSI companies including Bajaj Finserv, Protean, Ujjivan Small Finance Bank, Jana Small Finance Bank and Grihum Housing Finance.

Its models are designed to handle challenges such as background noise, overlapping speech, code switching and regional accents. The company has also collaborated with IISc Bengaluru, IIT Madras, Microsoft Research and the Gates Foundation.
The startup said its Bodhi speech model achieved the highest accuracy in a benchmarking exercise conducted across Indian voice AI platforms using real world speech samples.
Ronnie Screwvala said that Navana.ai is addressing the linguistic complexity of India and that voice AI could become a critical part of the country’s digital infrastructure. He also highlighted data localisation and regulatory compliance as key considerations for enterprise adoption.
Navana.ai is building voice AI infrastructure for regulated industries, with its Bodhi speech models being used by BFSI companies to serve customers in their own languages at scale.

title: Exclusive: Swish to raise around $24 Mn at $175 Mn valuation
summary:
Swish is raising fresh capital from Bertelsmann India Investments, adding a new institutional investor to its captable. The round comes just months after its last fundraise, pointing to continued investor interest in the emerging 10-minute food delivery model.
The Bengaluru-based startup is raising Rs 224.54 crore (around $24 million) in an extended Series B round led by Bertelsmann India, with the participation from its existing investors.
This will be the company’s second funding round this year. In March, Swish raised $38 million in a round led by Hara Global and Bain Capital.
The board at Swish has passed a special resolution to issue 4,123 Series B2 compulsory convertible preference shares at an issue price of Rs 5,44,616 each to raise the above mentioned amount, its regulatory filing accessed from the Registrar of Companies shows.
Bertelsmann India Investments will lead the round with an investment of Rs 143.34 crore ($15 million), joining Swish’s captable. Bain Capital Ventures will invest Rs 62 crore ($6.5 million), while Accel and Hara Global will participate with Rs 14.32 crore and Rs 4.8 crore, respectively.
According to the Entrackr’s estimates, Swish’s valuation will surge over 30% to Rs 1,653 crore or around $175 million post-money, from Rs 1,268 crore in its previous $38 million round.
Following the allotment of the new round, Bertelsmann India Investments will acquire an 8.67% stake in Swish. Accel will remain the largest shareholder with a 23.48% stake, followed by Hara Global with 17.93% and Bain Capital Ventures with 9.97%. Its co-founders Aniket Shah, Sureshkumar Saran and Ujjwal Sukheja will retain 10.98% each.
In June, Moneycontrol reported that Swish was in talks to raise $20 million from Bertelsmann India Investments. 
Founded in 2024, Swish operates a 10 minute food delivery model through a network of cloud kitchens located close to demand clusters. The company focuses on delivering meals within a limited radius to enable faster turnaround times. 
Prior to this round, the firm had raised around $54 million, including a $14 million round in March 2025, which was exclusively reported by Entrackr.
Launched in July 2024, Swish reported Rs 4 crore in revenue and a total loss of Rs 19 crore during the eight-month period of FY25. The company is yet to file its FY26 financial results.
Swish operates in a market that is no longer short of well-funded competitors. Blinkit’s Bistro, Zepto Cafe and Swiggy’s Bolt are already testing different approaches to faster food delivery, while cloud-kitchen players such as Rebel Foods and Curefoods add another layer of competition.
For Swish, the challenge will be to build enough order density and repeat demand to make its focused model work better than larger platforms with deeper distribution and existing consumer traffic.

title: Spactech startup Pixxel raises $100 Mn in Series C led by Temasek, Seraphim
summary:
Bengaluru-based space-tech startup Pixxel has raised $100 million in its Series C funding round co-led by Temasek and Seraphim Space.
The round also saw participation from new investors 360 ONE Asset and IMM Investment, along with existing backers Radical Ventures and growX Ventures, among others. The latest fundraise takes Pixxel’s total funding to $195 million. The company said the round is the largest funding raised by a space-tech company in India.
Media reports suggest that Pixxel is being valued at around $450-500 million in the latest round.
Pixxel will use the fresh capital to expand beyond hyperspectral imaging into advanced sensing satellites, Earth intelligence software, sovereign space systems and satellite manufacturing. Its plans include expanding the Honeybee constellation, developing high-resolution optical imaging satellites, scaling its Aurora Earth intelligence platform and increasing manufacturing capacity through Gigapixxel.
Founded by Awais Ahmed and Kshitij Khandelwal, Pixxel initially focused on hyperspectral imaging satellites and has since expanded into Earth intelligence software and satellite systems for commercial and sovereign missions.
Before the latest round, Pixxel had raised $95 million from investors including Google, Lightspeed, Radical Ventures, Blume Ventures, growX Ventures, Glade Brook Partners and Seraphim. The startup closed its Series B round at $60 million in December 2024.
The latest round comes shortly after Skyroot Aerospace became the first Indian space-tech startup to achieve unicorn status, crossing the $1 billion valuation mark.
Over the past two years, Pixxel has deployed six Firefly satellites, launched Aurora and secured contracts with NASA and the NRO. It has also won multiple iDEX challenges from the Ministry of Defence and was selected to lead the development of India’s first public-private Earth observation constellation of 12 satellites under IN-SPACe.

summary:
Electric two-wheeler maker Ola Electric has approved a plan to raise up to Rs 1,500 crore through the issuance of equity shares or convertible securities.
The company’s board approved the proposal on September 5. The fundraise can be carried out through a further public offer, rights issue, QIP, private placement or other permitted routes, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.
The development comes just three months after Ola raised Rs 780 crore through a QIP in June, when it allotted around 21.76 crore shares at Rs 35.86 apiece to qualified institutional buyers.
Meanwhile, Ola Electric COO Hyun Shik Park has resigned, effective from the closing business hours of September 5. The company said Park resigned from his role as a Senior Management Personnel due to personal reasons.
The fresh fundraise comes at a difficult time for the EV two-wheeler maker, which has been dealing with falling market share, customer complaints and a decline in its share price and market capitalisation.
In Q1 FY27, Ola Electric’s revenue from operations fell 45% YoY to Rs 455 crore, while its net loss narrowed to Rs 336 crore from Rs 428 crore a year earlier. The company recorded 13,170 vehicle registrations in July, giving it a 6.8% market share.
Ola Electric has also been scaling up its battery-cell manufacturing operations. It recently secured Rs 95.81 crore under the government’s PLI-Auto scheme for FY27.
The board has also approved increasing the company’s authorised share capital from Rs 8,318.5 crore to Rs 8,721.9 crore, subject to shareholder approval.

title: Rentomojo IPO: Early investors set for up to 152X returns through OFS
summary:
Rentomojo’s upcoming IPO is set to generate multi-fold returns for several of its early investors, with one shareholder set to clock a 152X return on its investment, while existing shareholders are looking to offload shares worth Rs 1,106 crore through the OFS.
According to Entrackr’s analysis, at the upper price band of Rs 404 per share, Accel India is set to generate around 8.63X returns on its Rs 317 crore OFS. Madison India could clock around 7.22X on its Rs 96.9 crore share sale, while ValueQuest and Edelweiss are expected to earn around 5.4X on their respective OFS shares worth Rs 109.6 crore and Rs 116.5 crore.
Chiratae Ventures is likely to generate around 4.93X returns on its Rs 194.1 crore OFS, while GMO could earn around 4.24X on its Rs 95.1 crore share sale.

Among individual shareholders, Nitish Mittersain, founder of Nazara Technologies, is set to emerge as one of the biggest beneficiaries. Mittersain’s investment in Rentomojo was his first startup investment. He is selling shares worth around Rs 6 crore through the OFS, which could fetch him around 152X returns based on the acquisition cost disclosed in the company’s offer documents and the upper IPO price band of Rs 404 per share.
Rajeev Chitrabhanu HUF is another notable early shareholder, with its Rs 12.4 crore OFS potentially generating around 26.6X returns.
The company’s founder Geetansh Bamania is set to offload shares worth Rs 34.3 crore, while other OFS participants include Japan-based Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance Venture Capital (MSIVC), Pratithi Investment Trust, Renaud Laplanche and others.
The returns are based on the weighted average acquisition cost disclosed in Rentomojo’s offer documents and the upper IPO price band of Rs 404 per share. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 150 crore and an OFS of around Rs 1,105.6 crore, giving the company a valuation of around Rs 4,200 crore at the upper band.
Rentomojo’s IPO is scheduled to open for subscription on September 9 and close on September 11.
Financially, Rentomojo has continued to grow while remaining profitable. Its revenue from operations rose 45.5% year-on-year to Rs 387 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 266 crore in FY25. Profit after tax jumped 142% to Rs 104.2 crore from Rs 43.1 crore in the previous fiscal.
